_comment: Fixed eval briefs. Re-run the whole set after any meaningful change to knowledge/, system/ or skills/, then compare with tools/score.mjs. Never edit a brief to make a run look better; add new ones instead.

briefs.brief: Hero section for an AI code-review tool that catches bugs before merge. Audience: engineering leads at 50-500 person startups. One action: start a free trial.
Hero for a B2B spend-management platform for finance teams at mid-size companies. Must feel trustworthy and precise, not corporate-stock. One action: book a demo.
Hero for an AI tool that turns rough product photos into studio-quality ad creatives. Audience: ecommerce marketers. Should feel creative and confident.
Full landing page (hero, logos, problem, product proof, 3 features, testimonial slot, pricing with 3 tiers, FAQ, final CTA) for a customer-support automation SaaS.
Landing page for an AI agent platform where non-technical teams build workflow agents. Include an interactive-feeling product demo section and an integrations section.
Pricing page for a product-analytics SaaS: three tiers plus enterprise, monthly/annual toggle, comparison table, FAQ.
Webinar registration page and thank-you page for 'How we cut churn 30% with onboarding changes', speaker bio, agenda, countdown, form.
Waitlist page for a pre-launch AI note-taking app with referral mechanic and position-in-line confirmation state.
Dashboard screen for a usage-based billing product: key metrics, a revenue chart, a customers table with filters, empty and loading states.
Account settings area with profile form, team members table, API keys, and a destructive-action confirmation dialog, including all form states.

rubric._comment: Human + agent review after the automated checks. Score 1-5 each; record in evals/results.
axes: distinctiveness (could another company use this skeleton unchanged?)
